I like problems where geometry, dynamics and manufacturing meet — the part has to fly, survive vibration, and still be buildable.

I completed my Master’s in Aerospace Engineering at Carleton University, specializing in rotorcraft stability, structural dynamics and simulation-based modelling. My graduate research, in collaboration with Bombardier, focused on understanding and mitigating whirl flutter in propeller-rotor systems using MATLAB and Maple.

Today I focus on mechanical design: parametric 3D models and assemblies in CATIA V5 and Fusion 360, production drawings with GD&T, and design-for-manufacturability backed by ANSYS and MATLAB analysis. Hands-on time maintaining CF6 engines at IR Airline, embedded-systems research at Akimbo Technologies and years of teaching CAD keep me designing for the people who make, inspect and maintain the part.

Speaking & teaching

Talks

Presenting research to industry engineers, defending it in front of a committee, and teaching it to the next cohort.

Invited talk· 2024

Propeller whirl flutter and aeroelastic stability in high-speed axial flight

Bombardier L&D Symposium 2024

Presented my research to Bombardier engineers and industry researchers: the physical principles of whirl flutter, and how quasisteady aerodynamic theory and the equations of motion reveal the stability dynamics of two-bladed rotors.

Thanks to the Bombardier L&D Symposium team and Gabriel Saiz for organizing.
Thesis defence· 2025

Whirl-flutter stability of two-bladed propeller-rotor systems

M.Sc. defence · Carleton University

Defended my Master’s thesis on rotor whirl flutter — modelling, stability analysis and mitigation strategies developed in collaboration with Bombardier.

Supervisors: Prof. Fred F. Afagh, Prof. Robert Langlois, Prof. Fidel Khouli
Committee: Prof. Jeremy Laliberte, Dr. Mehdi Eshaghi, Dr. Pakeeza Hafeez
